record.file_problem: Not garbled or cut off; the text contains repository metadata, README and file list only. Code was not read or run.
record.tranche_reason: Tests whether a rank-1 residual-stream projection changes refusal and sampled capabilities, but derives directions from checkpoint weight edits rather than harmful-minus-harmless mean activations.
record.gate_note: The README reports refusal and capability outcomes for the projection, including a negative-lambda addition. It also reports that the 128 applied directions are highly aligned. Candidate-selection values, implementation checks, serving-speed results, MTP acceptance results, and cited results are not rows because they do not measure the claimed refusal behaviour or general capability. The README explicitly says no GPU generation test was done for the proposed second axis, so it does not test whether refusal is multi-directional.
record.test_reason: The study measures refusal on StrongREJECT and trigger prompts, and benign-prompt refusal, while removing or adding a rank-1 direction at several strengths, with capability checks. That bears directly on V1 (removal, addition, abilities kept). It also bears on V2, because λ=1 reproduces a released abliterated checkpoint's weight edit (distance 1.5e-3 to the baked checkpoint). The direction comes from a base-vs-abliterated weight difference, not the study's own harmful-minus-harmless activation means, so this is T2 rather than T1.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors also say runtime projection at λ=1 is mathematically and empirically equivalent to the released Ektome abliterated checkpoint. In §4 they assert refusal is mediated by a single global direction. In §8.2, however, they argue the rank-1 structure is a property of the edit, not the model, since base weights show no dominant direction. They find a second near-orthogonal rank-1 axis but do not test what it controls.
record.recipe_differences: Uses rank-1 directions derived from checkpoint weight edits and applies them as runtime residual-stream projections, rather than extracting a harmful-minus-harmless mean-activation direction. The README cites the original paper as the method origin.
record.method_sensitivity: Projection strength changes both refusal and capability outcomes: refusals return near baseline at λ=2.5, while sampled quality declines at λ=1.5 and generation is invalid at λ=2.5. Negative λ increases benign refusals in the reported sweep.

fits_no_version.finding: The 128 edit directions are one vector (pairwise cos ≥0.9995, s0/s1=198). Yet base weights write along r_refusal only at chance (ρ≈0.014 vs 0.0140 random), and a separate roleplay edit (Queen) is a coherent rank-1 axis at |cos| 0.112 to r_refusal. No generation test was run.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The rank-1 structure of abliteration directions is imposed by the edit rather than found in the base model's weight geometry; models admit several near-orthogonal globally coherent rank-1 edit axes.

fits_no_version.finding: Of three published 'abliterated' Qwen3.8 checkpoints, only one is a clean rank-1 directional edit. The others have rank-1 energy 0.14–0.87 or 0.32–0.55, and one has λ_eff 2.599 (over-ablation).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Released 'abliterated' models often are not single-direction edits and vary in calibration.

record.problems: Repository evidence is README-only and code was not read or run. Refusal measurement uses 60 StrongREJECT prompts per arm, with ten examples per category; over-refusal prompts are enriched and are not representative-traffic estimates. Capability checks cover 100 GSM8K and 112 MMLU-Pro examples, plus an 8-item tool battery; the README says HumanEval and full benchmark suites were not run. The direction is not extracted by the original difference-in-means procedure.
record.rows_left_out: No other claim-relevant README results were left out. Serving-speed, compilation/runtime checks, MTP acceptance measurements, and candidate weight-delta geometry are not rows for the listed claim versions; the README also says no generation test was run for the proposed second axis.

untested.parts: Extraction of the direction as a harmful-minus-harmless difference in activation means. The direction here is taken from a third-party checkpoint's weight delta, and its provenance is not stated. Capability is sampled only (100 GSM8K, 112 MMLU-Pro, an 8-item tool battery); HumanEval and full suites were not run.
The authors did not create their own weight edit. Capability of the released edit is checked only through the equivalent runtime projection.
Jailbreak mechanisms and adversarial training against ablation.
Whether refusal is affine, conical or multi-directional. The second rank-1 axis found in §8.2 was never tested with generation.
Harmfulness judgment measured separately from the refusal decision.
Transfer across languages, variants or base-to-instruct. The over-refusal prompts are Spanish, but there is no cross-language comparison.
Effect of refusal training procedure or stage.

missing.what: Normal answers / disclaimers on StrongREJECT: λ=0 7/21, λ=1 56/4, λ=1.5 60/0, λ=2.5 11/20. At λ=1, 4 disclaimers remain, so removal of hedging is incomplete at the released edit.
Earlier 10-trigger smoke test: 5/5 refusals at λ=0 to 0/5 at λ=1 (repo description and §8.1 saturation note).

record.verdict_notes: This is README-only evidence from an engineering repository with small samples: 60 StrongREJECT prompts per arm, 4 triggers, 21 sweep samples. The direction's derivation is inherited from a third-party checkpoint, so the link to difference-in-means is assumed via the cited method origin. The study is not an original source.

versions.untested_parts: The direction was derived from checkpoint weight differences, not from harmful-minus-harmless instruction mean activations. Other abilities were sampled on GSM8K, MMLU-Pro and a tool-calling battery, not exhaustively tested.
The README tests runtime projection on a released base checkpoint and compares it with a baked ablation; it does not report creating and testing a separate weight-edited artifact.
No test of jailbreaks suppressing the direction or training against ablation.
No generation test establishing whether refusal is affine, conical, or carried by multiple refusal directions.
No separate measurement of harmfulness judgment and refusal decision.
No cross-language, model-variant, or base-to-instruct transfer test of the direction.
No comparison of refusal training procedures or training stages.

statements.correction: No correction needed. Optional detail: at λ=1 the outputs were 56 normal answers and 4 disclaimers out of 60. The base served was unsloth/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4. The hook matches the ideal projection to 7.9e-16, and the distance to the baked checkpoint is 1.5e-3 (BF16 floor).
statements.problem: Numbers and framing for this study are right: 32/60 → 0/60 strict StrongREJECT refusals at λ=1, 60 prompts per arm. The measurement is the runtime projection that reproduces the Ektome edit, not the Ektome checkpoint itself, and differences_stated says so.
